newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-EVERTON BOSS ROYLE LEAVES "BY MUTUAL CONSENT".
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-EVERTON BOSS ROYLE LEAVES "BY MUTUAL CONSENT".

text.p: Everton manager Joe Royle left the English premier league soccer club "by mutual consent" on Thursday.

The team's Clubcall line carried a statement from Royle which said: "I have been disappointed by recent results and by our current league position. Having spoken to the chairman I am leaving by mutual consent."

Royle, a former championship-winning hero as free-scoring centre forward with the club, made his managerial reputation with Oldham taking the unfashionable club into the then first division, League Cup final and F.A. Cup semis.
He returned to Goodison as manager in November 1994, replacing Mike Walker, and was a universally-welcomed choice.

Everton were wallowing at the bottom of the league and Royle immediately set about toughening them up. His combative no-nonsense approach, especially in midfield, led to his team being tagged the "Dogs of War."
They finished the season 15th of 22 clubs but with their first trophy in eight years after beating Manchester United 1-0 in the F.A. Cup final.

High hopes greeted the new season, especially after Royle bought Russian winger Andrei Kanchelskis for five million pounds ($8.1 million), and despite a poor European campaign, the club finished sixth in the league -- coming agonisingly close to a UEFA Cup place.

A flying start to this season had people talking of Everton as potential champions. However, a terrible run since Christmas, including just eight points from their last 13 games, have left them still not certain of avoiding another end-of-season relegation battle. They are currently in 13th.
Early exits in both cup competitions at the hands of lowly York and Bradford also caused massive disappointment to the Everton faithful.

Royle's surprise departure has led to speculation that another former player, Sunderland manager Peter Reid may take over. Reid was an integral part of the last great Everton team that won the title in 1985 and 1987 and reached three successive F.A. Cup finals from 1984-86.
Barcelona and former England boss Bobby Robson is another name in the frame.
The club said on Thursday it would make a general announcement "shortly" but that is not expected until Friday.
Millionaire chairman Peter Johnson may appoint a caretaker until the end of the season.
Johnson has already sent shock waves through the club by suggesting a move from Goodison Park -- its home for 105 years -- to a new purpose-built stadium on the outskirts of Liverpool.
Everton were one of the founder members of the football league in 1888 and have spent more years in the top flight than any other club.
They have won the league nine times and the F.A. Cup five times. Their only European success came in 1985 when they won the Cup Winners' Cup. ($ = 0.614 British Pounds)
